pr.title: Fix ACL key checks for SORT
pr.description: Sort command resolved ACL keys from a keyspec that didn't match the key the command actually operates on, allowing a permission bypass. STORE also uses last-wins semantics; the STORE keyspec is already `unknown`, so ACL falls back to `sortGetKeys()` -- but that parser didn't skip the STORE argument, so an earlier STORE value that looks like an option keyword (BY/GET/LIMIT) derailed the scan. Fixed the parser to skip the STORE argument so it isn't re-parsed as an option keyword; the last STORE still wins.

testCase.title: Background save completes successfully on a 32-bit Redis server once the dataset grows past a few megabytes
testCase.preconditions: A redis-server instance built for a 32-bit architecture is running in standalone mode with persistence enabled and no other background save currently in progress.
steps: Start a redis-server built for a 32-bit target architecture with default persistence (save points) enabled.
Insert keys until the in-memory dataset is large enough that the resulting RDB file would be a few megabytes.
Issue the BGSAVE command.
Wait for the background save to finish and check the server log and INFO persistence section.
testCase.expectedResult: The background save finishes and the log reports 'Background saving terminated successfully'; INFO persistence shows rdb_last_bgsave_status:ok and rdb_last_bgsave_time_sec with a non-negative value.

provenance.note: Issue #13671 ('redis rdb saving fails with signal 31 on 32bit machine - due to integer overflow?') opened 2024-11-28 and still OPEN as of 2026-08-16, with Redis collaborator sundb actively engaging on the thread (requesting repro data as recently as Jan 2025) without a fix landing. PR #15538 merged 2026-07-28 touches only src/db.c's sortGetKeys() ACL key-resolution parser and tests/unit/acl.tcl -- nowhere near the RDB background-save/fork code path (src/rdb.c, src/child.c) implicated in the open issue, so the background-save failure is present unchanged at both the PR's base and head revisions.

pr.title: fix(cwd): nvim_win_set_buf changes global CWD
pr.description: nvim_win_set_buf() on a non-current window, while the current window has a win-local dir, was changing the global CWD. `globaldir` is where to return when no local dir applies; switching to a window with no local dir made update_cwd() chdir back to `globaldir` and clear it, and kCtxKeepCwd restored the process CWD but not that bookkeeping, so the restored window-local dir was mistaken for the global one. Fixed by saving/restoring `globaldir` together with the CWD.

testCase.title: Incrementing a number under the cursor with CTRL-A preserves every digit when the number exceeds 64-bit range
testCase.preconditions: Neovim is running with an empty scratch buffer and default settings ('nrformats' includes decimal handling).
steps: Open a new empty buffer.
Type the number 12016012609141909200527091927191118250205120747 on a line by itself, then return to normal mode.
Move the cursor to the first character of that line.
Press CTRL-A to increment the number under the cursor.
testCase.expectedResult: The line now reads 12016012609141909200527091927191118250205120748 -- the original 50-digit number incremented by exactly one, with none of its digits lost, replaced, or otherwise altered.

provenance.note: Issue #3739 ('Increment and decrement operations truncate big numbers') opened 2015-11-24 and still OPEN as of 2026-08-16, with core contributors (e-kwsm, ZyX-I) confirming in-thread that the truncation to a 64-bit integer is a real, reproducible limitation of the CTRL-A/CTRL-X implementation. PR #41328 merged 2026-08-15 touches only src/nvim/context.c and context_defs.h (the temp-context CWD/globaldir save-restore machinery used by nvim_win_set_buf) plus its test spec -- entirely unrelated to the increment/decrement code in src/nvim/ops.c, so large-number truncation is unchanged at both the PR's base and head revisions.

pr.title: Fix race condition in reclaiming file cache blocks
pr.description: There was a race condition in reclaiming external file cache blocks: when a cached file's metadata was found stale, the code reset cache blocks in place even though another reader might already have pinned the same blocks and still need their byte counts, leading to an internal error such as 'FileBufferHandleGroup::CopyTo: handles contain N bytes but M were requested'. Fixed by adding RetireBlocks(), which removes only the matching map entries (without mutating blocks in place) so existing readers keep valid data while future reads fetch fresh blocks.

testCase.title: Concatenating an array literal with NULL using the || operator returns a NULL of the array's type
testCase.preconditions: A DuckDB instance (default settings) is available for querying via the CLI or a client library.
steps: Open a DuckDB connection (CLI or client library).
Run: SELECT [1] || NULL AS result;
Inspect the returned column's declared type and value.
testCase.expectedResult: The result column has an array type (INTEGER[]) holding a NULL array value -- the operator does not silently collapse the column to a scalar INTEGER type just because the NULL operand is untyped.

provenance.note: Issue #14692 ('list_concat([1], null) doesn't match [1] || null') opened 2024-11-04 and still OPEN as of 2026-08-16. DuckDB collaborator Mytherin confirmed in-thread: 'I agree this should not return a NULL type at all but rather return int32[]. I'll have a look at fixing this,' but no fix has landed. PR #24729 merged 2026-08-12 touches only the external file cache's block reclamation logic (src/storage/external_file_cache/*, its header, and its unit test) -- entirely unrelated to the list/array concatenation binder code, so the || / list_concat NULL type inconsistency is unchanged at both the PR's base and head revisions.

pr.title: [ScrollBar] Fix drag scrolling interfering with mouse on touchscreen
pr.description: ScrollBar's drag-scrolling logic is specifically meant for touch input and should only apply on touchscreens, but it was implemented on top of generic InputEventMouseButton/InputEventMouseMotion handling gated by DisplayServer::is_touchscreen_available(), which let touch-emulated mouse events interfere with real mouse dragging. Updated the logic to key off InputEventScreenTouch/InputEventScreenDrag directly (and skip emulated-device events) so it no longer interferes with mouse events.

testCase.title: A RefCounted subclass overriding _notification receives NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE while it is still a valid object
testCase.preconditions: A Godot project is open with a GDScript class defined that extends RefCounted and overrides _notification.
steps: Create a GDScript class that extends RefCounted and overrides _notification(what).
In the override, when what == NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE, print a message and read one of the object's own member variables.
Instantiate the class and store the instance in a local variable.
Set the local variable to null (or let it go out of scope) so the reference count drops to zero and the object is released.
testCase.expectedResult: The _notification override runs for NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE while `self` is still a valid, non-freed object, its member variable is read successfully, and the engine does not crash.

provenance.note: Issue #6784 ('Custom class instance extending Reference already freed when it receives NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE') opened 2016-10-11, labelled bug + confirmed, and still OPEN as of 2026-08-16 -- core team member KoBeWi and multiple other contributors discuss it as an unresolved, still-current limitation of RefCounted's predelete notification in the thread. PR #122255 merged 2026-08-10 touches only scene/gui/scroll_bar.cpp's touch-vs-mouse drag handling -- entirely unrelated to core/object.cpp or core/object/ref_counted.* where NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE is dispatched, so the predelete/freed-object issue is unchanged at both the PR's base and head revisions.

pr.title: FIX Raise error for categorical features with criterion='absolute_error'
pr.description: The categorical split-finding algorithm used by DecisionTreeRegressor/DecisionTreeClassifier is not valid for criterion='absolute_error': it can produce splits that aren't actually optimal for MAE. Rather than silently returning a possibly suboptimal split, DecisionTreeRegressor now raises a clear ValueError when categorical_features is combined with criterion='absolute_error', matching the other categorical-features incompatibility checks.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/doc/whats_new/upcoming_changes/sklearn.tree/33354.major-feature.rst b/doc/whats_new/upcoming_changes/sklearn.tree/33354.major-feature.rst
index 5a1a9bc0ffe26..645380032be14 100644
--- a/doc/whats_new/upcoming_changes/sklearn.tree/33354.major-feature.rst
+++ b/doc/whats_new/upcoming_changes/sklearn.tree/33354.major-feature.rst
@@ -1,6 +1,7 @@
 - :class:`tree.DecisionTreeRegressor`, :class:`tree.DecisionTreeClassifier`
   now have native support for categorical features for binary classification and
-  single-output regression. Categorical features can be specified with the
-  `categorical_features` parameter. Up to 256 categories per features are supported.
+  single-output regression. All criteria are supported except for `'absolute_error'`.
+  Categorical features can be specified with the `categorical_features` parameter.
+  Up to 256 categories per features are supported.
   By `:user:`Adam Li <adam2392>`, `:user:`Arthur Lacote <cakedev0>`,
   :user:`Adrin Jalali <adrinjalali>` and :user:`Christian Lorentzen <lorentzenchr>`
diff --git a/sklearn/tree/_classes.py b/sklearn/tree/_classes.py
index 862328768aa4b..80aed4f2f7be7 100644
--- a/sklearn/tree/_classes.py
+++ b/sklearn/tree/_classes.py
@@ -510,6 +510,11 @@ def _fit(
                 "Categorical features are only supported for binary classification. "
                 f"Found {self.n_classes_.max()} classes."
             )
+        if has_categorical and self.criterion == "absolute_error":
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Categorical features are not supported with "
+                "criterion='absolute_error'."
+            )
 
         SPLITTERS = SPARSE_SPLITTERS if issparse(X) else DENSE_SPLITTERS
         splitter = SPLITTERS[self.splitter](
@@ -1456,6 +1461,8 @@ class DecisionTreeRegressor(RegressorMixin, BaseDecisionTree):
         represented by ``np.nan``; unknown categories at prediction time are
         also treated as missing values.
 
+        Categorical features are not supported with `criterion="absolute_error"`.
+
         .. versionadded:: 1.10
 
     Attributes
diff --git a/sklearn/tree/tests/test_split.py b/sklearn/tree/tests/test_split.py
index 0df7f38eded9b..feea56f3d2b0f 100644
--- a/sklearn/tree/tests/test_split.py
+++ b/sklearn/tree/tests/test_split.py
@@ -247,6 +247,11 @@ def test_split_impurity(
 
     if categorical and "Extra" in Tree.__name__:
         pytest.skip("Categorical features not implemented for the random splitter")
+    if categorical and criterion == "absolute_error":
+        pytest.skip(
+            "absolute_error is not supported with categorical features in "
+            "DecisionTreeRegressor"
+        )
     rng = np.random.default_rng(global_random_seed)
 
     ns = [5] * 5 + [10] * 5 + [20, 30, 50, 100]
diff --git a/sklearn/tree/tests/test_tree.py b/sklearn/tree/tests/test_tree.py
index d7a3c395cd831..95c129797c550 100644
--- a/sklearn/tree/tests/test_tree.py
+++ b/sklearn/tree/tests/test_tree.py
@@ -2469,6 +2469,11 @@ def test_missing_values_best_splitter_on_equal_nodes_no_missing(
     criterion, categorical_features
 ):
     """Check missing values goes to correct node during predictions."""
+    if categorical_features is not None and criterion == "absolute_error":
+        pytest.skip(
+            "absolute_error is not supported with categorical features in "
+            "DecisionTreeRegressor"
+        )
     X = np.array([[0, 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 11, 12, 15]]).T
     y = np.array([0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2, 1.4, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 2.6])
     node_value_func = np.median if criterion == "absolute_error" else np.mean
@@ -3136,6 +3141,22 @@ def test_fit_categorical_with_monotonic_constraint(Tree):
         Tree(categorical_features=[0], monotonic_cst=[1], random_state=0).fit(X, y)
 
 
+def test_fit_categorical_with_absolute_error():
+    # Non-regression test: the categorical split-finding algorithm is not
+    # valid for criterion="absolute_error" (see gh-34578), so it should be
+    # rejected rather than silently return a possibly suboptimal split.
+    X = np.array([[0.0], [1.0], [0.0], [1.0]], dtype=np.float64)
+    y = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0])
+
+    with pytest.raises(
+        ValueError,
+        match="Categorical features are not supported with criterion='absolute_error'",
+    ):
+        DecisionTreeRegressor(categorical_features=[0], criterion="absolute_error").fit(
+            X, y
+        )
+
+
 def test_predict_sparse_int64_indices_raises():
     X = np.array([[0.0], [1.0]], dtype=np.float64)
     y = np.array([0, 1])

testCase.title: f_regression returns a valid, finite F-score for a constant feature column instead of NaN
testCase.preconditions: scikit-learn is installed and importable; a feature matrix and target vector are prepared in memory as described in the steps.
steps: Construct a feature matrix X with one constant column (the same value in every row) and at least one column that varies, plus a numeric target vector y.
Call sklearn.feature_selection.f_regression(X, y).
Inspect the returned F-statistic and p-value for the constant column, and check for any warnings raised during the call.
testCase.expectedResult: The function returns a finite F-statistic of 0.0 and a p-value of 1.0 for the constant column (it carries no linear information), with no RuntimeWarning about an invalid value encountered in sqrt and no NaN in the output.

provenance.note: Issue #11395 ('f_regression takes square root of negative values when constant columns are present') opened 2018-06-30 and still OPEN as of 2026-08-16. Maintainer agramfort acknowledged it in 2018 with a candidate fix commit that was never merged, and contributor Lawson-Darrow confirmed on 2026-06-03 (comment: 'This still reproduces on main') that r_regression's `sqrt(row_norms(X.T, squared=True) - n_samples * X_means**2)` still hits catastrophic cancellation for constant columns. PR #34594 merged 2026-07-30 touches only sklearn/tree/_classes.py (DecisionTreeRegressor's categorical-features validation) and its tests/changelog -- entirely unrelated to sklearn/feature_selection/_univariate_selection.py, so the f_regression/r_regression NaN-on-constant-column defect is unchanged at both the PR's base and head revisions.

testCase.title: r_regression does not emit a sqrt-of-negative-number warning for a near-constant column
testCase.preconditions: scikit-learn is installed and importable; a feature matrix and target vector are prepared in memory as described in the steps.
steps: Construct a feature matrix X containing one column with extremely low variance (values differing only in the last few significant digits) alongside a normally varying column, plus a target vector y.
Call sklearn.feature_selection.r_regression(X, y) while capturing warnings.
Inspect the returned correlation value for the near-constant column.
testCase.expectedResult: No RuntimeWarning is raised during the call, and the correlation value returned for the near-constant column is a valid finite number within [-1, 1] rather than NaN.

provenance.note: Issue #11395 ('f_regression takes square root of negative values when constant columns are present') opened 2018-06-30 and still OPEN as of 2026-08-16. pr.title: UI: Swagger input fix
pr.description: The Open API explorer's swagger-ui component added a readonly attribute to disabled form fields to address an accessibility concern, but never removed it once a field became enabled again, leaving those inputs unable to accept input. Updated updateDisabledFields() to remove the readonly attribute once an element is no longer disabled, only applying it while the element is actually disabled.

pr.title: sql: fix FETCH FIRST on empty WITH HOLD cursor
pr.description: FETCH FIRST on a persisted WITH HOLD cursor over an empty result set returned an internal error ('decoding unset EncDatum') instead of zero rows. In fetchMoveNodeBase.nextInternal, the FetchFirst branch for curRow == 0 discarded the bool returned by sqlCursor.Next and unconditionally reported a row, so the caller tried to decode an unset EncDatum. Fixed by propagating Next's (more, err) directly from the case 0 branch, matching the FetchAbsolute path just below.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/pkg/sql/logictest/testdata/logic_test/cursor b/pkg/sql/logictest/testdata/logic_test/cursor
index 896b07e5f0e2..dba02eca4620 100644
--- a/pkg/sql/logictest/testdata/logic_test/cursor
+++ b/pkg/sql/logictest/testdata/logic_test/cursor
@@ -943,3 +943,20 @@ statement ok
 CLOSE foo;
 
 subtest end
+
+# Regression test for FETCH FIRST on a persisted WITH HOLD cursor over an
+# empty result set returning an internal error instead of zero rows (#171238).
+subtest regression_171238
+
+statement ok
+BEGIN;
+DECLARE foo_first CURSOR WITH HOLD FOR SELECT * FROM empty;
+COMMIT;
+
+query empty
+FETCH FIRST FROM foo_first;
+
+statement ok
+CLOSE foo_first;
+
+subtest end
diff --git a/pkg/sql/sql_cursor.go b/pkg/sql/sql_cursor.go
index 4436ed3fdceb..1496e2b552c2 100644
--- a/pkg/sql/sql_cursor.go
+++ b/pkg/sql/sql_cursor.go
@@ -288,8 +288,8 @@ func (b *fetchMoveNodeBase) nextInternal(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
 		case tree.FetchFirst:
 			switch b.cursor.curRow {
 			case 0:
-				_, err := b.cursor.Next(ctx)
-				return true, err
+				more, err := b.cursor.Next(ctx)
+				return more, err
 			case 1:
 				return true, nil
 			}

testCase.title: Comparing an INET value against a set of subnets using <<= ANY succeeds
testCase.preconditions: A CockroachDB cluster is running and reachable via the SQL shell; the session has no special settings that would restrict INET type usage.
steps: Connect to a CockroachDB cluster's SQL shell.
Execute: SELECT INET '192.168.1.5' <<= ANY (SELECT INET '192.168.1.0/24');
testCase.expectedResult: The statement parses and executes without error, returning true (the address is contained within or equal to the subnet on the right-hand side).

metadata.feature: INET special operators with ANY/SOME/ALL subqueries

provenance.note: Issue #24495 ('sql: INET special operators do not work with ANY') opened 2018-04-05, labelled C-bug, and still OPEN as of 2026-08-16. Contributor knz confirmed in 2021 ('This is an outright syntax bug which is still present in 21.1') and a user reconfirmed in 2022 on CockroachDB 22.1.0; grepping the current pkg/sql/parser/sql.y grammar shows subquery_op's all_op production still omits INET_CONTAINS_OR_EQUALS/INET_CONTAINED_BY_OR_EQUALS, so `<<=`/`>>=` still cannot be combined with ANY/SOME/ALL. PR #171337 merged 2026-06-10 touches only pkg/sql/sql_cursor.go's FETCH FIRST cursor-advance logic and a cursor logic-test file -- entirely unrelated to the SQL grammar/parser, so the INET-operator-with-ANY syntax error is unchanged at both the PR's base and head revisions.
